incidents.vector: Abused Dropbox's integration with Lenovo's identity service, registering Lenovo ID accounts with victims' email addresses and bypassing email verification to pivot into matching Dropbox accounts.
incidents.impact: Data downloaded from almost 5,000 Dropbox accounts in August; breach disclosed this week.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion into the streaming service's systems in early June 2026.
incidents.impact: Personal data of almost 40 million user accounts stolen, spanning more than 70 types of personal details including names, emails, and phone numbers; company faces a regulatory fine for late reporting.

incidents.vector: Voice-phishing calls to employees, then stolen credentials used to take over Okta single sign-on accounts.
incidents.impact: Extortion group claims theft of 284 million patient records; McKesson is managing fallout from the data theft extortion attack.

incidents.vector: Password spraying, vishing, insider recruitment, rogue hardware planted in retail networks, and malware staged on compromised government websites to reach payment systems such as Pix.
incidents.impact: Fraudulent instant-payment transactions issued directly to attacker accounts — hundreds of transactions within 24-48 hours of access in one case, stealing tens of thousands of dollars; tactics now spreading to other countries.

incidents.victim: US and Canadian court systems (via Thomson Reuters C-Track)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the C-Track court case management platform operated by a Thomson Reuters subsidiary, undetected from March until June 30.
incidents.impact: Sealed court information and personal data (SSNs, driver's licenses, medical data) exposed for courts in at least 12 US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Canada.

incidents.victim: Latin American government, water, transport and financial organizations
incidents.vector: Two AI-assisted campaigns: living-off-the-land intrusions with LLM-generated scripts against Mexican and Ecuadorian government and utility targets, and job-themed phishing with custom RATs and SOCKS5 tunnels against Brazilian financial firms.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data manipulated and exfiltrated from a Mexican transportation organization, federal ministries and municipal water utilities; Brazilian financial sector intrusions ongoing with attacker-hosted AI chat interfaces orchestrating operations.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Breach of the ATF's lawful-access (CALEA) system by a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service group.
incidents.impact: 6.3 GB of claimed stolen data briefly published, including case folders with names, phone numbers, and IP addresses of investigation targets and mobile phone forensic data; ATF confirmed it is investigating.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two zero-days (CVE-2026-83548 SSRF, CVSS 10, and CVE-2026-83549 command injection) chained for unauthenticated remote code execution on edge remote-access appliances.
incidents.impact: Attackers gain significant control of internet-facing remote access gateways; SonicWall urges immediate patching, IOC review, re-imaging of compromised appliances, and credential resets. Added to CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: External Teams chats and calls impersonating IT helpdesk staff to obtain a remote-assistance session, then silent MSI install of a Node.js-based implant.
incidents.impact: Persistent backdoor with screenshot capture, Active Directory reconnaissance, and lateral movement toward domain controllers — a precursor pattern to data theft and ransomware deployment.

incidents.vector: Breached a public API endpoint, then used autonomous AI agents to map the network, harvest secrets, hijack CI/CD pipelines, and seize cloud AI infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Weeks of intrusion tradecraft compressed into under 10 hours; source repositories raided, root credentials seized, and the victim's AI compute turned into attacker infrastructure before ransom negotiation.

incidents.vector: Mass password-recovery attack against hundreds of thousands of accounts, apparently aiming to capture accounts linked to the new X Money banking service.
incidents.impact: Attack disrupted by X engineers; no confirmed account compromises, and the Justice Department is pursuing the attackers.

incidents.vector: Exploiting poorly secured VPNs, internet-facing applications, and credentials stolen from business partners to deploy custom ransomware, loaders, and a security-killing tool.
incidents.impact: At least seven Russian organizations hit with custom ransomware and multimillion-dollar ransom demands; stolen data may also be published or reused in further attacks.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the company's Amazon Web Services infrastructure between December 2 and 18, 2025.
incidents.impact: More than 9.5 million people's names, SSNs, medical and financial data stolen, affecting patients of at least 30 healthcare organizations; scope disclosed to regulators this week.

incidents.vector: Commercial spyware infections — one via a zero-click exploit, others apparently installed while devices were in police custody.
incidents.impact: At least 14 people targeted including a member of parliament and student pro-democracy activists — the largest documented spyware wave in Serbia to date; victims alerted by Apple notifications.

incidents.victim: Russian civil-society fundraisers (Davayte, You Are Not Alone)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal or Russian state suspected
incidents.vector: Compromise of the Stripe-WooCommerce payment integration used for online auctions in mid-August.
incidents.impact: Donor email addresses and partial card data exposed for projects supporting Ukrainians and Russian political prisoners — data that could expose donors to prosecution under Russian law.

incidents.vector: Voice-phishing attack against employees to gain network access and steal internal documents.
incidents.impact: More than 7,200 bank and credit union customers notified of the breach; the company says it will not pay the ransom.

incidents.vector: Apparent long-running breach of a major identity verification provider, with document scans continuously exfiltrated for over a year and sold via a dark-web service.
incidents.impact: Digital scans of 153M+ US and Canadian driver's licenses (including senior US officials') offered for sale, with roughly 400,000 new records added daily; FBI has opened an inquiry.

incidents.vector: 20-year-old polymorphic file-infector botnet using peer-to-peer command and control to deliver cryptocurrency clipboard-hijacking malware.
incidents.impact: Botnet disrupted August 31 by CrowdStrike, DOJ, FBI, Europol and partners via peer-to-peer sinkholing; at least $150,000 in cryptocurrency stolen over its lifetime, operator remains at large.

incidents.vector: Compromise of Coder's Cloudflare infrastructure to add rogue registry servers delivering malicious Terraform modules.
incidents.impact: Malicious registries live for 14 hours on August 31, exposing customers deploying cloud infrastructure for AI applications to poisoned modules.

incidents.vector: Exploited a bug in the underlying Cosmos blockchain platform, previously used against six other platforms.
incidents.impact: $74 million initially stolen of a $75 million attempt; $68 million clawed back, and Cosmos halted activity pending a fix.

incidents.vector: 33-hour BGP hijack of part of Hetzner's IP space, with a fraudulently obtained TLS certificate and a cloned website serving malicious updates for the VPS management platform.
incidents.impact: Unknown number of hosting providers received malicious Virtualizor updates; payment data submitted during the window likely stolen, and hijacked traffic passed entirely through attacker infrastructure.

incidents.victim: European government, diplomatic and defense organizations
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures to install a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command and control.
incidents.impact: Initial-access campaigns against government and diplomatic targets in Romania, Spain, and Türkiye from September 2025 through April 2026, supporting Russian intelligence collection including around Moldova's elections.
